# Phase One — Boundless Every-Page Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos is one beyond all routes while every route receives an exact vessel and voice;
Awtsmoos.com can become one coherent civilization without forcing every page into one identical choice.

## Unlimited Possibilities

1. Generate a canonical public-route registry from real `geelooy` entries and distinguish fixtures/templates/internal tools.
2. Give every route a health record: load, console, network, MIME, overflow, focus, labels, touch targets, fixed-layer collisions, empty render regions, timings.
3. Test desktop, tablet, 430px phone, and short-height behavior where the route family permits.
4. Define family acceptance contracts instead of treating documents, games, editors, social flows, and media as identical.
5. Search: hydration, submit, options, loading, results, empty/error, history, deep links, provenance, phone keyboard.
6. Social: create/read/edit/publish, preview, validation, draft persistence, auth boundaries, responsive composition.
7. Games: first playable frame, controls, movement, objective progress, restart, win/fail, resize, input claims, frame pressure.
8. Editors: canvas initialization, asset load, tool response, timeline/properties, resize, empty-state clarity, failure recovery.
9. Media: play/pause/seek, captions where present, loading/error, controls, poster sizing, lazy loading.
10. Libraries/docs: readable measure, navigation, search, deep links, mobile overflow, source provenance.
11. Auth/account: clear state, disabled/error/success/focus flows, no secret exposure.
12. Indexes: functioning apps/games discoverable; incomplete experiments labelled truthfully.
13. Shared shell changes only after multiple routes prove a common root defect.
14. Reuse existing Civilization tokens/components only when evidence says they improve the family.
15. Performance budgets by family: content/interaction ready time, request count, transfer bytes, long tasks.
16. Dynamic compact transport for JS/CSS only after semantics, latency, MIME, cache, and byte gains are proven.
17. Remove duplicated critical-path resources where ownership permits.
18. Defer non-primary context, media, editor, or game subsystems until first interaction is usable.
19. Maintain a route-debt ledger linking symptom, source owner, evidence, fix, tests, browser proof, production proof.
20. Work in verified tranches: search/content, indexes, social, apps/editors, games, media/auth/docs, long tail.
21. Use active-agent claims as concurrency boundaries, not just dirty-file status.
22. Rerun the full matrix after every tranche.
23. Keep source readable while server transport may compact dynamically.
24. Treat keyboard, focus-visible, labels, zoom, reduced motion, touch size as ordinary functionality.
25. Treat loading speed as functionality.
26. Prefer truthful experimental labels over pretending prototypes are finished.
27. Measure production after deploy, not only localhost.
28. Allow follow-up release commits if safe concurrent changes land during verification.
29. Never reset/stash/clean other agents' work merely to simplify the diff.
30. Continue until the route ledger contains no remaining safe relevant defect.

## Architectures

A. Global CSS rewrite — reject: cascade/concurrency blast radius.
B. Route-by-route bespoke repair — useful but can duplicate patterns.
C. Family contracts + route-local implementation — preferred balance.
D. Runtime-gate-only — strong evidence but insufficient for subjective clutter alone.
E. Shared component rewrite first — defer until repeated root-cause evidence exists.

## Preferred Synthesis

C + D + targeted B: family quality contracts, runtime measurement, route-local complete-file reconstruction, and shared changes only when multiple independent traces demand them.

## NEXT_ACTION

Map family verification contracts and concurrency boundaries, then perform a Phase Two critique before any new production-file edits.
